25910-the-long-portage.title: The Long Portage
25910-the-long-portage.creator: Harold Bindloss
25910-the-long-portage.description: A book by Harold Bindloss. Vernon Lisle was fishing with a determination that did not spring altogether from love of the sport. The water of the British Columbian river in which he stood knee-deep was icy cold; his rubber boots were badly ripped and leaky, and he was wet with the drizzle that drove down the lonely valley.

arxiv-2411-17979.title: GRADIENT FLOW OF PHASE TRANSITIONS WITH FIXED CONTACT ANGLE
arxiv-2411-17979.creator: KOBE MARSHALL-STEVENS, MAYU TAKADA, YOSHIHIRO TONEGAWA, & MYLES WORKMAN
arxiv-2411-17979.description: Abstract We study the gradient flow of the Allen–Cahn equation with fixed boundary contact angle in Euclidean domains for initial data with bounded energy. Under general assumptions, we establish both interior and boundary convergence properties for the solutions and associated energy measures.

arxiv-2501-00865.title: Negative Co-learning to Positive Co-learning with Aggressive Modality Drop
arxiv-2501-00865.creator: Nicholas Magal, Minh Tran, Riku Arakawa, Suzanne Nie
arxiv-2501-00865.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Nicholas Magal, Minh Tran, Riku Arakawa, Suzanne Nie. This paper aims to document an effective way to improve multimodal co-learning by using aggressive modality dropout. We find that by using aggressive modality dropout we are able to reverse negative co-learning (NCL) to positive co-learning (PCL). Aggressive modality dropout can be used to ’prep’ a multimodal model for unimodal deployment, and dramatically increases model performance during negative co-learning, where during some experiments we saw a 20% gain in accuracy.

pmc-11429490.title: Therapeutic inertia and contributing factors among ambulatory patients with hypertension
pmc-11429490.creator: Yirga Legesse Niriayo, Solomon Girmay, Nigusse Tesfay, Kidu Gidey, Solomon Weldegebreal Asgedom
pmc-11429490.description: BackgroundTherapeutic inertia refers to the failure of healthcare providers to initiate or intensify therapy based on current evidence-based guidelines, even when the desired treatment goal is not achieved. Despite poorly controlled hypertension, clinicians often hesitate to intensify treatment. Therapeutic inertia is currently receiving more attention as a significant reason for clinicians’ inability to effectively manage hypertension.

pmc-11494155.title: Long‐term outcome of 2‐year survivors after allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplantation for acute leukemia
pmc-11494155.creator: Marion Larue, Myriam Labopin, Thomas Schroeder, Xiao‐jun Huang, Igor W Blau, Johannes Schetelig, Arnold Ganser, Rose‐Marie Hamladji, Wolfgang Bethge, Nicolaus Kröger, Gerard Socié, Urpu Salmenniemi, Henrik Sengeloev, Bhagirathbhai Dholaria, Bipin N Savani, Arnon Nagler, Fabio Ciceri, Mohamad Mohty
pmc-11494155.description: Information on late complications in patients with acute leukemia who have undergone allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplantation (HCT) is limited. We performed a left‐truncated analysis of long‐term survival in patients with acute leukemia who were alive and disease‐free 2 years after HCT.

pmc-12401143.description: ensity on the periphery. Detail of an axial CT scan of the chest, showing a mediastinal lymph node of normal dimensions (arrows), with a hypodense center (mean density = −80 HU) and a halo with greater, homogeneously thick density on the periphery. Central hypodensity in lymph nodes may be a normal finding or correspond to a series of pathological conditions.

pmc-12495762.title: GRP-based vaccines as a novel approach in cancer immunotherapy: mechanisms, challenges, and prospects
pmc-12495762.creator: Razieh Malekian Shahreza, Hamed Zare, Nima Rastegar-Pouyani, Hamid Aria, Fatemeh Hakim, Mohammad Arefnia, Hamid Bakherad
pmc-12495762.description: Glucose-regulated proteins (GRPs), key members of the heat shock protein (HSP) family, function as molecular chaperones that are upregulated under endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress. Prominent GRPs such as GRP78, GRP94/gp96, GRP75, and GRP170 play a great role in cancer cell survival and progression by promoting protein folding, immune evasion, and resistance to therapy.

pmc-12503872.title: Intrahepatic Cholangiocarcinoma in Wilson’s Disease: 2 Case Reports
pmc-12503872.creator: Joana Reis Aguiar, Helena Pessegueiro Miranda, Cláudia Pereira
pmc-12503872.description: IntroductionWilson’s disease is a rare autosomal recessive inherited disorder of human copper metabolism. The spectrum of clinical manifestations of liver disease ranges from asymptomatic to cirrhosis and acute liver failure. Unlike the increased frequency of hepatobiliary tumours in other chronic liver diseases, the incidence of these tumours in Wilson’s disease is an uncommon event, even in cirrhotic patients.

pmc-12650536.title: First Evidence of Anti-Plasmodium vivax (Plasmodiidae): Activity of the Essential Oil and 6-Ishwarone Isolated from Piper alatipetiolatum Yunck. (Piperaceae)
pmc-12650536.creator: Glenda Quaresma Ramos, Renata Galvão de Azevedo, André Correa de Oliveira, Maria Luiza Lima da Costa, Felipe Moura Araujo da Silva, Ingrity Suelen Costa Sá, Gisely Cardoso de Melo, Stefanie Costa Pinto Lopes, Gemilson Soares Pontes, Sergio Massayoshi Nunomura, Rita de Cássia Saraiva Nunomura, Rosema
pmc-12650536.description: Background/Objectives: In the Brazilian Amazon, which accounts for over 99% of national malaria cases, 34,260 cases were reported as of August 2025, predominantly caused by Plasmodium vivax, responsible for 86.69% of the infections. The increasing resistance of the parasite to conventional therapies highlights the urgent need for novel control strategies, with essential oils and plant-derived substances emerging as promising alternatives.

pmc-13235442.title: Migration of a cutter knife blade into the abdominal aorta following penetrating chest trauma: A case report
pmc-13235442.creator: Masashi Kabasawa, Masao Hirano, Hiroki Ikeuchi, Mitsuru Aoki, Kozo Matsuo
pmc-13235442.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). We report a rare case of intravascular migration of a cutter knife blade after penetrating chest trauma. A 40-year-old man presented with lower abdominal pain 3 months after an unreported occupational injury to the left anterior chest wall. Computed tomography scan revealed a plate-like foreign body embedded in the distal abdominal aorta and a localized hematoma adjacent to the cardiac apex. The blade was successfully removed during semi-emergent abdominal aortic replacement.

pmc-13283667.title: Beyond Technique: Does Graft Sizing Relative to Notch Size Predict Arthrofibrosis in Young ACL Patients?
pmc-13283667.creator: Adam Nasreddine, Emma Gossman, Madeline McGovern, Chilan Leite, Benton Heyworth, Mininder Kocher
pmc-13283667.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Background:Arthrofibrosis (AF) is a common and, at times debilitating, complication following anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction (ACLR), which may necessitate unexpected additional procedures, including arthroscopic lysis of adhesions (LoA) and manipulation under anesthesia (MUA). Its reported incidence varies widely (2-35%), with published risk factors including early ACLR following injury, female sex, younger age, specific autograft type, such as patellar or quadriceps tendon, and concurrent meniscal repair.

pmc-13479084.title: Exploring Participation as a Mechanism of Domain-Specific Learning During Otolaryngology Clinical Clerkships
pmc-13479084.creator: Teruyuki Sato, Kaoru Toshima, Fumi Shishido, Yutaka Tateda, Takahiro Suzuki, Naoya Noguchi, Muneharu Yamazaki, Akina Shirotori, Fumi Shoji, Shunsuke Kawamoto, Hirohito Metoki, Tomomitsu Miyasaka, Isao Ohno, Yoko Shimotani, Takaaki Tanaka, Nobuo Ohta, Yutaka Nakamura
pmc-13479084.description: BackgroundClinical clerkships are a form of workplace-based learning in which authentic participation is considered a key contributor to learning. However, it remains unclear which domains of clinical learning depend on authentic participation and which can be supported through structured instructional activities.

pmc-13565868.title: Vitamin D and COVID-19: Inmunomodulatory Effects and the Mexican Public Health Perspectives
pmc-13565868.creator: María Luisa Muñoz-Almaguer, Erick Yair Flores-Salas, Carlos Bancalari-Organista, Raymundo Escutia-Gutierrez, María Virgen-Montelongo, Felipe Alexis Avalos-Salgado, Esmeralda Marisol Franco-Torres, Ana Montserrat Corona-España
pmc-13565868.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Vitamin D is a fat-soluble vitamin, considered a prohormone, that plays a fundamental role in calcium absorption and reabsorption, as well as the modulation of inflammatory response in infectious conditions such as COVID-19. A literature search was conducted in scientific databases and official sources, selecting studies published in the last 10 years in Spanish and English related to vitamin D and COVID-19; studies unrelated to the nutritional approach were excluded to reduce bias and ensure a rigorous and reproducible analysis.

pmc-13573496.title: Necroptosis in alveolar epithelium orchestrates lung ischemia-reperfusion injury: a multi-omics study
pmc-13573496.creator: Fuxiang Liang, Tong Wang, Zhiling Lou, Jinsheng Li, Huan Yu, Zhijie Xu, Yifan Yu, Xiaolong Hu, Xiaofang Xu, Yongchao Wang, Yaling Chen, Weiping Zhang, Yunbi Lu, Ming Wu
pmc-13573496.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundLung ischemia-reperfusion injury (LIRI) is a leading cause of early morbidity and mortality following lung transplantation and other cardiopulmonary procedures. It is characterized by acute sterile inflammation driven by regulated cell death (RCD).

pmc-13576789.title: Polycationic Peptide Engineering of Phage Endolysins Expands Host Range and Enhances Antibacterial and Antibiofilm Activities Against Bacillus Species
pmc-13576789.creator: Farhat Ansari, Tarushi, Vandan Nagar
pmc-13576789.description: The exponential rise in antimicrobial resistance has highlighted the urgent need for the development of alternative antibacterial strategies, including phage‐derived and engineered protein agents such as endolysins and artilysins. In this study, we report the rational design, expression, and functional characterization of novel artilysins derived from P19_358 lysin, a glycoside hydrolase family 24 enzyme.
